question: What becomes possible when machines can read a whole library as easily as a page?
reflection: Cheaper ways to understand vast knowledge could open research to many more curious minds.

sources.subject: Latent Sparse Attention Speeds Up 10M-Token AI Contexts by 9x

one_line: Researchers found a cheaper way for AI models to search very long inputs, which could make agents that work for hours on huge document sets more affordable.

top_stories.title: A library-style shortcut for very long AI inputs
top_stories.what: Researchers at Prefrontal AI and ETH Zurich describe Latent Sparse Attention, which sorts a model's memory into clusters so it only searches the most promising ones, reportedly cutting the wait for a first answer by up to nine times on 10-million-token tasks.
top_stories.why: Research projects often mean feeding AI thousands of interview transcripts or policy documents at once, and lower costs at that scale make such analysis practical.

top_stories.title: Open code lets teams test it now
top_stories.what: The team released the code and ready-made add-ons for two open models under a permissive licence, while noting the speed gains shrink on shorter inputs and one model lost some accuracy.
top_stories.why: An in-house data team could test it on a real archive before paying for a commercial long-context service.

saudi_lens.text: No direct Saudi link today. Indirectly, cheaper long-context processing on open models helps organisations that must keep large Arabic archives on local servers.

idea.title: Whole-archive question answering
idea.pitch: Load a full archive of past survey reports into one long-context open model and test whether it answers cross-year questions as well as a human analyst.
idea.fit: Culture sector, labour-market agency, consultancy knowledge management
idea.first_step: Pick ten questions that need facts from several old reports and record how long a person takes to answer them.

idea_kids.title: The giant library treasure hunt
idea_kids.pitch: A puzzle book where children learn to find answers in a big library using an index, keywords and clues, the same idea AI uses to search long texts.
idea_kids.first_step: Choose 5 questions and hide the clues across a pretend library map.

watchlist.name: Prefrontal AI
watchlist.note: Co-developed Latent Sparse Attention and published the code openly.

verify: Reported speed-ups of 9 times for first-token time come from the researchers' own tests on 10-million-token tasks and may be far smaller on normal inputs.

terms.definition: How much text, code or data an AI model can take in and consider at one time.
A way for an AI model to look only at the most relevant parts of its input instead of every word, which saves time and computing power.
How long you wait before an AI model starts producing its answer.

concepts.summary: Techniques that make it cheaper for models to work with very large inputs.
Agents that work for hours or days and build up huge working memories.
